summary: The paragraph is faithful in outline but has several errors of fact and reading: the section numbers are 172 and 176 (not 272/276); פירש is 'separated' not 'explained'; אלפין are alefs, and the two verses 1 Kgs 7:26 and 2 Chr 4:5 were left unidentified; מספר יהי אור is 'the number of Let there be light' (232), not a book; the Deut verse is 30:8 verbatim and several verses (Isa 32:15, Neh 6:8, Gen 46:1, Exod 19:21) were unrecognised while an Avot reference was added against the ruling. Quotation marks around the Menorat ha-Ma'or passages were broken, fragments began in lower case, and 'lore', 'own' and 'that' were added. The open points are decided from context: the Chavot Yair quotation ends at 267, העליון is 'the above-mentioned', לי"ח is conjecturally 'to the initiates', לחשוב is 'to think' after 'break through', סדר is left as 'Seder'.

patches.value: Have you seen, to know the words of the Gaon Chavot Yair, how afraid and trembling he is to teach about separation, and relies on the words of the Gaon, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, whose words were cited above, yet he is still afraid to say it outright, lest it slacken the hands from engaging in this holy wisdom, and how much he praises this wisdom, for one who merits it, to learn it from the mouth of a Kabbalist, and admits that anyone who holds himself back from studying it, after receiving it, is pushed away from his precinct; and also he permits engaging in the words of Kabbalah, and if he sees puzzling things before him, he should accept them in the faith of an artisan, and attribute it to the shortness of his understanding. If so, your two witnesses, the Ribash and Chavot Yair, will testify and bear witness against you that you invent things from your own heart; and where is his separation, that he separated, as you said? Did he not himself say, "Would that a spirit from on high were poured upon us," etc.? And I bring you proof that he merited the wisdom of Kabbalah, for in section 172 he wrote, and these are his words: "that it is possible there are further matters of secret and concealment in two verses, 'two thousand bath it held' and 'three thousand baths,' for at the sin of the first man three alefs were corrupted, of truth, of Adonai and of man, and there remained mat-din-dam against idolatry, illicit unions and bloodshed. And King David repaired truth; therefore he did not taste sleep at night, and did not manage to repair judgment, and also blood, as the Holy One, blessed be He, said: 'You shall not build the house, for you have shed much blood; only your son Solomon, for peace, etc.' And Solomon repaired two alefs, and with the alef of his father, three alefs were repaired, and the matter of bat is known to the initiates, for the main flaw is there, and he further expanded on the secret of the matter there. And section 176, on the matter of one who feeds a man blind in one of his eyes, and with all this I protested, for it seems to me that in both cases there is room to distinguish. However, where there is another fitting and suitable one like him, for it is known that the 248 limbs are a throne and a likeness of the 248 supernal lights, and the 248 limbs of the soul. And so, in every such case the throne is flawed, for according to the hidden there are heaps upon heaps of secret mysteries in the parts of the body, and there is a lack of flow in the cup of blessing." The above-mentioned, too, in the colophon of the book, wrote that he made 635 responsa and gathered from them 232, the number of "Let there be light," and it has the gematria of the four fillings of YHVH, 72, 63, 45, 52: the son who is in Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva. And further, "Let there be light" is Yah ya'ir ("Yah will give light"). These are the sources of Tif'eret (Beauty) and Malkhut (Kingship) in Binah (Understanding), which is the light emanated on the first day. And he further expanded on many matters of secret and concealment. Also his father, the author of Shemen la-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for his verses were printed at the end of the book. And these are according to the Name of forty-two, and the twelve combinations of YHVH, and the twenty-four combinations of Adonai, and the Name of twenty-two. Also the true sage, the author of Menorat ha-Ma'or, was a divine Kabbalist, for in chapter 93 he wrote on "Baruch She'amar": "its way in it, the number of the ten, the ten, etc." And in chapter 95 he wrote: "Kaddish is not said with fewer than ten, and the reason is that with ten the holiness is completed, which is above the ten sefirot." And in chapter 133 he wrote: "When Jacob was going down to Egypt, he saw that the exile had begun in him and in his seed, and he feared it and sacrificed sacrifices to the Fear of his father Isaac, so that the attribute of judgment would not be stretched out against him; and did this at Beersheba, which is a house of prayer for his fathers, and offered peace-offerings to complete to him all the attributes, as they expounded: 'shelamim, which cast peace', to complete to him the attribute of Gevurah (Might)." And in chapter 147 he wrote: "It is found that the completeness of holiness is in the ten, which allude to the ten havayot, and they are the ten sayings by which the world was created." And in chapter 153 he wrote: "And in the way of truth, that in six days the LORD made, etc. and on the seventh day it is Sabbath, and it has no male mate, and the Assembly of Israel is its female mate, as it is said: 'and the earth,' and behold, it is the Eighth Day of Assembly, for there everything is held back. And this is their saying: 'The eighth is a festival in itself,' and it is the completion of the first, for it is the emanation of the first ones, and it is not in their unity, and whoever understands the havayot will be wise and find the truth." And in the colophon of the book he wrote: "And the fifth, I left out the grave matters, which are hidden and lofty, and there is no one who can attain them but a single individual in a generation." Thus he wished to write secret matters in his work, but because they are not fit for every person. Have you seen, to know that no one disputes the Kabbalah: neither the early ones nor the later ones, neither the many nor the individuals, neither the great nor the small. On the contrary, all agree that whoever merits Kabbalah from mouth to ear, there is no finer virtue for you than it, and that it is forbidden to expound and investigate it; but if he wishes, he should accept it in complete faith and not explain it by his human intellect. For he should attribute what troubles him to the shortness of his understanding, and not break through to think anything of the soul. And with this, all the words of the lowest of the low are complete. Seder. And you shall return and listen to the voice of the LORD.
patches.reason: Section numbers are 172 and 176 (קע"ב, קע"ו), not 272/276, and external sections are 'section', not '§'. פירש in 'פרישתו שפירש' is 'separated', not 'explained'. אלפין are alefs (the letters), not 'alafin'; the two verses are 1 Kgs 7:26 and 2 Chr 4:5 ('two thousand bath it held', 'three thousand baths'). לדזכי is Aramaic 'for one who merits it'; ממחיצתו is 'his' precinct. מספר יהי אור is 'the number of "Let there be light"' (232, the point of the gematria), not a book title; תשובות is 'responsa'; יה יאיר is 'Yah will give light'. 'Lore' and 'own' are added; 'that' in the Baruch She'amar quotation is added. The Menorat ha-Ma'or quotations are closed where they end (chapter 95 and 153 ran past their closing marks), with nested single marks and capitals fixed; בן זוג / בת זוגו keep male/female; ותשלומי ראשון הוא כי הוא is 'it is the completion of the first, for it is the emanation of the first ones'; 'and the earth' is the end of Exod 20:11 and 'and behold' is the author's; שמיני רגל has no 'Day'; fragments joined (ruling on אם...או / full stops); קבלה kept as 'Kabbalah'; פ' + numeral is 'chapter' (ruling: numeral exceeds any parashot count); יהרוס לחשוב is 'break through to think' (Exod 19:21,24); סדר is left as 'Seder'; 'hearken' modernised.

patches.reason: The new English changed the fragments; each still occurs in the English, in order.
לדזכי is Aramaic d-zakei 'who merits', not an infinitive 'to merit'.

patches.value: Aramaic dezakei, 'who merits'; the ל is 'for': 'for one who merits it, to learn it from a Kabbalist'. The reading lizkot ('to merit') is in readings.
patches.reason: Note matches the gloss.
ממחיצתו is masculine, 'his' (חכמה is feminine, so not 'its').

patches.value: 'his precinct': the Hebrew does not say whose (the one who holds back, or the Kabbalists'); it is not 'its', which would be ממחיצתה.
patches.reason: Learner note.
פירש after פרישתו is 'separated' (root פרש), the abstention at issue.

patches.value: pirash, 'separated', from the root of פרישתו and הפרישה; the unpointed word could also be piresh 'explained', but the question is where his abstention is.
patches.reason: Learner note.

patches.value: the author's truncated quotation; the wording echoes Isa 32:15 (עד יערה עלינו רוח ממרום), which is the likely source
patches.reason: The verse is Isa 32:15 and can be verified; 'not verified' was wrong.

patches.value: the letters kuf-ayin-bet, 172; a section of Chavot Yair
patches.reason: Learner note.
דאלפים בת יכיל is 1 Kgs 7:26, 'two thousand bath it held'; it is a verse, not a Kabbalistic designation.

patches.value: Aramaic d-, 'that of'; 1 Kgs 7:26 (the Sea of Solomon). The author also reads alafim as 'two alefs'.
patches.reason: Learner note.
Bath, the liquid measure (a homograph of bat, 'daughter').

patches.value: a liquid measure; the same letters are bat 'daughter', the term the author takes up below
patches.reason: Learner note.
יכיל is 'it held', part of the verse.
וג' is 'and three' (gimel as a numeral), not the letter name.

patches.value: gimel used as the number 3, for 'three thousand'
patches.reason: Learner note.
אלפים here is 'thousand(s)' in the verse; the author also hears 'two/three alefs'.

patches.value: alafim 'thousands'; the author's play is on alef, the letter (see the grammar note)
patches.reason: Learner note.
בת' is the abbreviated בתים 'baths' (2 Chr 4:5 in the author's wording).
אלפין is the Aramaic plural of אלף, the letter: the three alefs of אמת, אדנות, אדם.

patches.value: plural of alef, the letter; the alefs that begin emet, adnut and adam
patches.reason: Learner note.

patches.value: what is left of אמת, אדנות and אדם without the alef: mat 'dead', din 'judgment', dam 'blood'; kept as printed, hyphenated
patches.reason: Explains the exegesis (ruling on exegesis that turns on a Hebrew word).

The quotation from Chavot Yair is opened by כתב וז"ל (115-116) and runs to 267; it includes the passage on section 176, whose 'I protested' (213) is the Gaon's own voice. The Holy One's words inside it (164-179) take single marks. The next sentence (268 on) is the author's own report.

לדזכי לה ללמדה (41-43): דזכי is Aramaic, 'who merits': 'for one who merits it, to learn it from the mouth of a Kabbalist'. פרישתו שפירש (90-91): the verb is pirash 'separated', of the same root as הפרישה (13).

The exegesis at 123-148 turns on alef: אלפין is the Aramaic plural of אלף, the letter. The three alefs are the first letters of אמת, אדנות and אדם; without them what remains is מת, דין and דם, 'mat-din-dam', set against idolatry, illicit unions and bloodshed. The two verses (1 Kgs 7:26, 2 Chr 4:5) speak of 'two thousand' and 'three thousand' baths; the author hears אלפים as 'two alefs'. בת is both the measure 'bath' and 'bat', 'daughter'.
שמיני רגל (488) is the Talmudic formula for the Eighth Day, which is Shemini Atzeret (481); the author argues from its separateness to the emanation of the first ones.
ולא יהרוס לחשוב (592-593): 'break through to think', as in Exod 19:21, 24; the sentence after a full stop that begins with שהם (300) is given a main clause ('These are'), as the ruling provides.
patches.reason: The old notes mentioned §272 and a conditional list; these notes carry the points a learner needs (the alef exegesis, the Aramaic, the verb).

Quotation boundaries: the Chavot Yair quotation, opened by כתב וז"ל (115-116), is taken to run from שאפשר (117) to the cup of blessing (267), including the passage on section 176; the Hebrew marks no closing formula, and the end is inferred because 268 (העליון ג"כ ... כ') resumes the author's own report. The quotations from Menorat ha-Ma'or have no formula either; each is closed where its passage ends.
Neh 6:8: מלבך אתה בודאם, echoed in בודה דברים מלבך (85-87).
Isa 32:15: עד יערה עלינו רוח ממרום, echoed in the Gaon's מי יתן ויערה עלינו רוח ממרום (98-103), in the author's wording.
1 Kgs 7:26: אלפים בת יכיל (125-127); 2 Chr 4:5 for 'three thousand baths' (128-130), in the author's wording, which differs from the verse.
1 Chr 22:8-9: the words 'לא תבנה הבית כי דמים רבים שפכת, רק בנך שלמה כי שלום' follow the author's wording, which differs from the verse.
Gen 1:3: יהי אור (280-281, 296-297), the phrase whose number is 232.
Gen 31:42: פחד יצחק, 'Fear of Isaac' as a divine epithet (400-402); Gen 46:1: ויזבח זבחים (398-399).
Exod 20:11: ששת ימים עשה ה' (457-460), cut short with וכו' (461); ואת הארץ (476-477) is the end of the same verse.
Exod 19:21, 24: פן יהרסו / ואל יהרסו, a possible echo in ולא יהרוס לחשוב (592-593).
Deut 30:8: ואתה תשוב ושמעת בקול ה' (603-607), exactly as the verse reads.
